artworks.title: The Devotion of Menoeceus, the Son of Creon
artworks.description: Leslie’s Edwardian sculpture stages Creon’s son offering himself to Ares so Thebes may stand against the Seven — the willing death Euripides and Statius make the city’s price. Rare modern art that names Menoeceus apart from his grandfather.

popCulture.title: Phoenician Women
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides’ Theban play sends Menoeceus to voluntary death for the city’s salvation — the tragic hinge of Creon’s house before the brothers’ duel.

popCulture.title: Thebaid
popCulture.creator: Statius
popCulture.description: Statius expands Menoeceus’ self-sacrifice into a Latin epic set-piece — the son of Creon as Thebes’ chosen victim before the Argive assault.
